# Template: hydraulic_press
A hydraulic press / lift / jack in cross-section: two connected cylinders of different bore joined by a fluid-filled channel, a small input piston pushed down by a force arrow and a wide output piston carrying a load block, with area labels (A₁, A₂), force labels, an optional displacement mark (d₁ down, d₂ = d₁/ratio up) and an optional pressure equation P = F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂. Choose this scene for any request about hydraulic presses, hydraulic lifts, jacks, brakes, Pascal's principle / Pascal's law, pressure transmitted equally through a fluid, force multiplication, or 'why can a small force lift a heavy load'. The piston width ratio follows √(area ratio), since the drawing is a cross-section of round cylinders.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "areaRatio": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "Output piston area divided by input piston area, A₂/A₁ (default 4). Clamped to 1.2–12 for drawability; the drawn bore ratio is its square root."
  },
  "inputForce": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "Numeric value of the input force applied to the small piston (default 100). Output force is shown as inputForce × areaRatio."
  },
  "forceUnit": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Unit shown after force values (default \"N\")."
  },
  "showValues": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Show numeric force values and the numeric area relation (default true). Set false for a purely symbolic figure with just F₁, F₂, A₁, A₂."
  },
  "inputLabel": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Symbol for the input force (default \"F₁\")."
  },
  "outputLabel": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Symbol for the output force / lifted load (default \"F₂\")."
  },
  "smallAreaLabel": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Label for the small piston area (default \"A₁\")."
  },
  "largeAreaLabel": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Label for the large piston area (default \"A₂\")."
  },
  "loadLabel": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Text written inside the load block on the big piston (default \"Load\"; e.g. \"Car\", \"1000 kg\")."
  },
  "fluidLabel": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Label for the fluid in the connecting channel (default \"Incompressible fluid\"). Empty string hides it."
  },
  "title": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Optional caption across the top of the figure (e.g. \"Hydraulic jack\"). Empty by default."
  },
  "showDisplacement": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Show the displacement marks: the small piston travels d₁ down while the large piston rises only d₂ = d₁/ratio (default false). Use it when explaining that work is conserved."
  },
  "showEquation": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Show the pressure equation lines P = F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂ (and the numeric output force) at the top (default true)."
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- ground / ground_line: hatched ground the press rests on
- vessel_outer / vessel_inner: the two walls of the connected cylinders
- fluid: the shaded fluid filling the channel and both bores
- piston_small / piston_small_fill: the narrow input piston
- rod_small / plate_small: the input piston rod and its push plate
- piston_large / piston_large_fill: the wide output piston
- load / load_fill / load_text: the load block resting on the big piston
- force_in: the downward input force arrow
- force_out: the upward output force arrow above the load
- displacement: group of dashed levels and d₁/d₂ travel arrows (optional)
- eq_pressure / eq_force / eq_dist: the pressure, force and distance equation lines
- title: optional caption
- label_force_in / label_force_out / label_area_small / label_area_large / label_fluid / label_d1 / label_d2: the collision-solved name labels
Examples:
Request: "Draw a hydraulic press and show why a small force can lift a heavy load." → params: {}
Request: "Explain Pascal's principle with a hydraulic jack lifting a car: 50 N input, area ratio 10, show the distances each piston moves." → params: {"areaRatio":10,"inputForce":50,"loadLabel":"Car","showDisplacement":true,"title":"Hydraulic jack"}

In YAML: `template: hydraulic_press` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
